whatItIs: NaturesMud Dehydrated Mango is made from tree-ripened sweet Nepali mangoes harvested at peak summer sweetness from Terai orchards. Each mango is hand-peeled, sliced into thick cheeks, and slowly dehydrated at low temperatures. Unlike imported supermarket dried mango that is boiled in white sugar syrup and gassed with sulphur dioxide (E220), our mango slices have 0% added sugar, 0% sulphur, and 0% preservatives.

whoItSuits: Perfect for children, students, trekkers, fitness enthusiasts, and anyone who loves the taste of ripe Nepali summer mangoes year-round without refined sugar coatings.
monsoonStorage: Because our mango slices contain zero sulphur preservatives, keep the ziplock pouch sealed tightly after opening. During warm and humid monsoon months, storing the opened pouch in the refrigerator keeps the slices firm and prevents darkening.

faqs.q: What is the price of Dehydrated Mango (सुकेको आँप) in Nepal?
faqs.a: NaturesMud Dehydrated Mango (100 GM Pouch) costs Rs. 595 in Nepal (Rs. 595 per 100g). Approximately 800g–1kg of fresh ripe mangoes go into making a single 100 GM pack.

faqs.q: Why is NaturesMud Dehydrated Mango deep amber-orange instead of bright neon yellow?
faqs.a: Bright neon-yellow dried mango sold in supermarkets is treated with sulphur dioxide (E220) bleach and sugar syrup. Because we use 0% sulphur and 0% sugar, our ripe mango slices turn a natural rich amber-gold as they dry.

faqs.q: Does it have any added sugar or salt?
faqs.a: None at all. The ingredients list is simply 100% ripe mango. All sweetness comes naturally from the fruit itself.

faqs.q: Can kids eat Dehydrated Mango in their school tiffin?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a favorite chewy fruit snack for school-age children (for toddlers, cut into small bite-sized strips).

faqs.q: How should I store the pouch after opening?
faqs.a: Press the ziplock seal shut firmly after each use and store in a cool cupboard or refrigerator away from heat and moisture.
